briefs.claim_en: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission became the first to land in the lunar south pole region on August 23, 2023.
briefs.brief_en: Multiple sources confirm that India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed near the Moon's south pole on August 23, 2023. NASA Science, The Guardian, PBS, Sky & Telescope, and Space.com all report this event, with some specifying the landing time around 6:04 p.m. Indian Standard Time (IST) or 12:34 GMT. A fact check by BOOM Fact Check also refutes claims that China was the first to land on the lunar south pole, reinforcing India's achievement as the first. NDTV also reported the scheduled landing for August 23, 2023, at approximately 18:04 IST.

briefs.claim_en: The Vikram lander from Chandrayaan-3 successfully touched down at 18:04 local time (12:34 GMT) on August 23, 2023.
briefs.brief_en: Various sources confirm that the Vikram lander from India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully touched down on the Moon on August 23, 2023. NDTV and Space.com reported the scheduled landing time as approximately 18:04 IST (12:34 GMT). Wikipedia states the landing occurred at 18:04 IST (12:33 UTC). Sky & Telescope specifies the landing at 12:34 Universal Time (UT), while PBS reported it at 6:04 local time. The Guardian also noted the Vikram lander touched down shortly after 6 p.m. (1230 BST) on the same date.

briefs.claim_en: India joined the US, the former Soviet Union, and China in achieving a soft landing on the Moon on August 23, 2023.
briefs.brief_en: Multiple news outlets and encyclopedic sources confirm that India became the fourth country to achieve a soft landing on the Moon on August 23, 2023. The Business Standard, Wikipedia, PBS, Space.com, Sky & Telescope, and India TV News all report that India joined the United States, the former Soviet Union (or Russia), and China in this accomplishment.
